content:
Hello. I heard that a collaborative editing feature had been added to Lean 4 Web, so I tried it with a friend, but we couldn’t get it to work at all. Could this be a bug?

I can connect two accounts from the same PC, but it doesn’t seem possible to edit simultaneously with someone using a different device.
@Jon Eugster I think you are a maintainer of lean4web
Also, as a feature request, I’d like the ability to generate an invitation link after creating a room so that I can invite friends to join it.

Jon maintains lean4web but not the version deployed to live.lean-lang.org. I'm not sure why pulling in the feature into our branch (announced here #general > lean4 web collaborative @ 💬 — you might try the https://lean.math.hhu.de/ deployment to see if that works for you better) didn't work, but in the meantime I've backed out of the change, removing the collaborate feature from live.lean-lang.org. Thanks for letting us know it wasn't working — if the lean.math.hhu.de version does not work for you, that _is_ definitely something @Jon Eugster should know about.

Thank you! lean.math.hhu.de works for me!

but I have a feature request.

When three or more people join, some participants are assigned the same color. Could you make the cursor colors as distinct as possible?
the collaboration feature should be correctly (re)deployed on live.lean-lang.org now if you want to check.
Hmm, I'm struggling to get either of them working. I'm joining the room Test with no password from both my phone and computer with different display names. Am I failing to do something necessary?

Shoot. I'm on the road and unable to debug, but that should be all you need to do. (You're sure you're on live.lean-lang.org for both?)

If the feature isn't stable I'll disable it on live.lean-lang.org until it matures on lean.math.hhu.de, I'm sorry you're having a bad experience.

No worries! I’m excited to see it grow :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:I did make sure I was on live.lean-lang.org in both places, then tried again with lean.math.hhu.de in both places.

Happy to share more info/act as a test subject to help debug when you’re back if it would help! I think this’ll be cool to use during the Meta Café. :)

Thomas Murrills said:

I think this’ll be cool to use during the Meta Café. :)

I don't know how live-lean works for you, but for me the server (or the client connection to it) gets stuck every ~1 minute and I have to refresh the page, and this has always been the case. Whenever I work in live-lean I hit Ctrl+R every ~30 seconds.
This might depend on geographical location, idk.

FWIW VSCode has such a sharing feature. I have never tested it with the Lean extension though.
(it's also sometimes unreliable, but IME the time-until-it-breaks is much more than 1 minute)

I've been discussing a similar issue with @Jason Reed over the last few days - good to know I'm not the only one. To make sure these aren't different issues though, does it resolve after ~1 minute of waiting while keeping the tab open?

I think so, yes, but refreshing solves it faster.
Just to be clear:

  • This has forever been the case for me, so for at least a year
  • This is not a complaint to live-lean: I think the issue is money for more servers (or money for devs to get Lean working in Wasm again, or observability/autoscaling/etc), and this is a free community service. I just wanted to raise the issue with regards to using it in the Meta Café.

it always happens right after an edit, and the amount of time it gets stuck seems to depends on how much I was typing and how much file there is, but I have had cases where it gets stuck for longer than I have the patience to wait for

I happened to record a video earlier today showing something like this happening: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrKlLNumORM. For example, at 1:14 I make an edit to the file, and I only get updated diagnostics at around 2:23. The example is mathematically trivially false, and grind usually is very quick to solve it, so taking over a minute for Lean to respond feels quite surprising and frustrating
Since we're on the subject, see also upvotes on this message: #general > live.lean-lang.org indefinitely waiting @ 💬 (but the topic itself is unrelated I believe)

Bhavik Mehta said:

I happened to record a video earlier today showing something like this happening: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrKlLNumORM. For example, at 1:14 I make an edit to the file, and I only get updated diagnostics at around 2:23. The example is mathematically trivially false, and grind usually is very quick to solve it, so taking over a minute for Lean to respond feels quite surprising and frustrating

@Jason Reed has diagnosed this and merged an initial fix - if you try again on live.lean-lang.org, things should behave a bit better.

The issue, it turned out, is head-of-line blocking: responses from the server can get 'stuck' behind other, large responses when the large response has already begun streaming. The bad sequence of events in your video is likely: 1) VSCode requests completions for 'a' or 'b' 2) server replies with completions - with import Mathlib, the list of matches for a single letter is 20-40MiB (and this is already with some information omitted to minimize size) 3) reply starts streaming to the browser 4) you make some changes 5) server elaborates them and send 'elaboration done', 'new tactic state' notifications. While the reply 3) is still streaming, the notifications 5) are stuck and the infoview shows the loading spinner.

Ideally the connection would have out-of-order delivery/multiplexing so that the small high-priority notifications can arrive before the completions do, but WebSockets do not support this afaik. For now, we have a partial fix in lean4web#133 which tells the server to compress anything above 16MiB. There are fewer bytes to transfer, so the completions arrive and unblock updates more quickly, e.g. completions for 'c' get compressed from 28MiB to just 4MiB.
I'm hearing that compressing completions isn't fixing the symptom on bhaviks end though so more investigation is required
Are completions for single letters helpful? If VSCode isn’t using additional context, a suggestion based on a single letter seems a bit premature.

That is not an ideal assumption. If everybody thinks this way an problem tends to get much lower priority or attention compared to filed issues. Hoping for a problem to just resolve itself might work in projects where there are enough contributors with spare capacity to doodle around. Even if it's just a condensed summary of a zulip chat, an issue (generally for any inconvenience) is still very helpful, even more so if it contains some reproducable #mwe :)
